The Person Behind the Research

About Me

I am an incoming Aerospace Engineering student at SRM Institute of Science and Technology (SRMIST), Kattankulathur Campus, beginning my B.Tech in 2026. Alongside this, I work as a Research Intern at exovista, contributing to astronomy and space science research, and I founded The Redshift Asterism in June 2026 — an independent publication where I write research-driven articles on cosmology and astrophysics for a general audience. I also contribute to NASA-affiliated open science work through Zooniverse and the Open Science Data Repository (OSDR) Analysis Working Group.

Current Work

My technical work centres on Python — building applications like a Streamlit-based RPG with branching state logic and a CLI task manager with persistent CSV storage — and on the mathematics behind cosmology and orbital mechanics. At exovista, that translates into data analysis and contributing to collaborative research workflows. At The Redshift Asterism, it means converting research literature on topics like black holes, dark matter, and the origins of the universe into writing that holds up to scrutiny without losing readability.

Long-Term Direction

Working toward graduate research in astrophysics or aerospace systems, with computational methods for studying space as the connecting thread — using the engineering side of my degree to understand how spacecraft and instruments are built, and the computing side to model and analyse what they observe. The Summer School of Rocket Science this July is a step toward that.

Philosophy

How I Approach Work

I.

When a problem is unfamiliar — a new physics framework, an unfamiliar Streamlit API, a research question with no clear starting point — I start by mapping what is already known and where the gaps are, rather than guessing at a solution.

II.

I learn new technical material by building with it immediately rather than finishing a course first. This usually means early versions are rough, but it surfaces the parts of a concept that documentation alone doesn't make obvious.

III.

I separate the question of whether something works from the question of whether it's built well: get a working version, then rebuild the parts that won't scale.

Technical Projects

Programming applied to research, logic design, and computational problem-solving — the first of more to come once coursework begins.

◆

RPG Mini Game

Python · Streamlit · State Logic

A stat-allocation game where players distribute points across Strength, Intelligence, and Charisma to unlock one of three hidden legendary archetypes — first built as a CLI tool, later rebuilt as a Streamlit web app.

Read the build notes
Problem

The original CLI version mixed game logic with print statements, making it impossible to reuse the logic in a different interface.

Approach

Rewrote the archetype logic as pure functions independent of display; Streamlit's session state handles persistence between reruns.

Lessons

Separating logic from presentation early made the rebuild straightforward — the hardest part was relearning state management for a framework that doesn't keep variables alive between runs.

Play Live ↗View Code ↗
◇

Task Tracker

Python · CSV I/O · CLI Design

A command-line task manager that stores tasks with priorities and due dates in a CSV file, built to understand file I/O and data persistence in Python directly.

Read the build notes
Approach

Used Python's csv module with a fixed schema read into memory on launch and rewritten on every change. CRUD operations sort by priority before display.

Known limitation

Rewriting the entire CSV on every edit is inefficient at scale and risks data loss if the program exits mid-write.
